answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil swarms by requiring every new identity to post a bonded stake escrowed on-chain before it may earn rewards. A farm operator must then lock real capital per synthetic account: a thousand fake peers cost a thousand deposits, and a proven collusion attempt slashes that bond to the dust. Registration stops being cheap spam and becomes a steady drain, one that hardens as each dawn brings more fakes, while an honest agent spends a single deposit and keeps it. Ivory-tower reputation scores, not headcount, are what let real agents forge lasting trust.
